clue.text: Two pounds in supermarket for a slice of meat, in some places

definitions.text: a slice of meat, in some places

indicators.note: in places the two pounds inside the name of the shop

parts.note: the Co-op is a British supermarket chain
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two pounds is LL

explanation.surface: A shopper at the supermarket pays two pounds for a slice of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British chain of grocery stores. 'in some places' marks the definition as a regional word.
explanation.definitionFit: A collop is a dialect word, mostly Scots and northern English, for a thin slice or escalope of meat.

clue.text: Symbol of vote — in short, X — for entertainer

indicators.note: in short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper
X is read as 'by', as in multiplication, 3 x 4

explanation.surface: A voting mark, an X in short, given for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bing Crosby was an American singer and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bing Crosby was a famous American crooner and film star, an entertainer of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Awfully clear to me that person's been held up?

definitions.note: a phrase meaning someone who has been delayed, standing for the noun

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: It is terribly obvious that someone was delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' suggests a robbery; here it means delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer is someone who arrives after the expected time, typically because they were delayed.

clue.text: Play round, then relax with opponents at table

parts.note: O is round in shape
to rest is to relax
at the bridge table East and South are opponents, E and S

explanation.surface: A card player: play a round, then unwind with your opponents at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, players are named by compass points; East and South sit on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes is a Greek tragedy by Euripides, named after Agamemnon's son.

clue.text: Culture in which commander and king embrace Hindu music?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first pair of words hold the music between them

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander or official
R is short for rex, Latin for king
a raga is a pattern of notes in Indian classical music

explanation.surface: A cultural scene where a commander and a king enjoy Hindu music together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Culture' looks like arts and music, which the surface plays up, but here it means a laboratory growth medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is the seaweed jelly used as a medium for growing bacterial cultures in laboratories.

clue.text: Information on horrendous king, shah or emperor

indicators.note: on means placed above, in a down clue the first piece sits on top

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: horrendous means awful, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Intelligence on a horrible monarch, a shah or emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British informal for information. Shah and king look like extra definitions alongside emperor, but they are anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Genghis Khan founded the Mongol Empire and ruled it as its great khan, or emperor.

clue.text: Violent tirade involving a politician

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the tirade wraps round what follows

parts.note: a rant is a tirade
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A furious outburst that drags in a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant can mean unrestrained and fierce, as in rampant aggression.

clue.text: Annoyed with rubbish at end of game

indicators.note: at end of places the rubbish after the game

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by the junk left over at the end of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got at is to be nagged, criticised or harassed, which leaves one annoyed.

clue.text: Regret when daughter is hauled in before head for bad behaviour

indicators.note: before means this comes ahead of the next piece
hauled in means pulled inside, so the daughter goes into the regret

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A parent regrets their daughter being hauled before the head for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a head teacher; it is a headland, NESS, as in Loch Ness's shores or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is impolite or offensive conduct, a kind of bad manners.

clue.text: Beginning anything but a trendy clique?

parts.note: the opposite of in (trendy) is out
a set is a social group or clique

explanation.surface: A question about starting off as the very opposite of a fashionable crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A trendy clique is an 'in set'; anything but that is an OUT SET.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset of something is its start or commencement.

clue.text: Partner in a nest on fire

indicators.note: in tells us the partner sits within the other letters

parts.note: a nid (or nide) is a nest, especially of pheasants
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A bird's partner in a nest that has caught fire.
explanation.walkthrough: NID is an old word for a pheasant's nest; the partner goes between A and its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, someone on fire is full of energy and passion, which is what animated means.

clue.text: Incisive projections?

parts.note: incisive is read as relating to incisors, the front teeth, and projections as things that stick out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Incisive' normally means sharp or penetrating, as in criticism; here it plays on incisors, the cutting front teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Protruding upper front teeth are literally projections of the incisors.

clue.text: Ten leaders I fancy will be given immortal status?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imagined, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten leaders I imagine will be made immortal.
explanation.definitionFit: To eternalise something is to make it last forever, conferring everlasting fame.

clue.text: University little short of a gem

indicators.note: a little short means a word just missing its last letter

parts.note: a stone is a gem

explanation.surface: A university that falls just short of being a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Aston University is in Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston is the name of a British university in Birmingham.

clue.text: They must be repeatedly smart with sea being rough, these officers?

indicators.note: a rough sea is choppy and disturbed, so these letters are churned up

parts.note: repeatedly says the word smart is used a second time
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Naval officers must stay smart, even when the sea is rough.
explanation.walkthrough: SMART SMART SEA is rearranged; the clue hints at naval discipline, fitting the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A master-at-arms is a ship's police officer responsible for discipline aboard naval vessels.

clue.text: Engineers certain to go after a record again

indicators.note: to go after places this piece behind what comes before

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Engineers are sure to chase a record once more.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a corps of the British Army. 'record' looks like a disc; with 'again' it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To remeasure is to take and note a measurement a second time.

clue.text: Went up and addressed Greek island, performed to entertain it

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the performance holds the island inside

parts.note: acted means performed
Kos, also spelt Cos, is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone approached and spoke to a Greek island, performing to amuse it.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and speak to them, often boldly.

clue.text: RHS chum may net hybridised flowering plant

indicators.note: hybridised plants are crossed and mixed, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend from the Royal Horticultural Society might bag a hybrid bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The RHS is the Royal Horticultural Society, Britain's gardening charity, which fits the gardening picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a popular garden and florist's bloom of the daisy family.

clue.text: Groundbreaking symposium given a change of direction

indicators.note: right becomes left: the R standing for right is swapped for L for left

parts.note: a seminar is a symposium or discussion meeting

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking conference that takes a new direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work is highly influential, strongly shaping later developments.

clue.text: Traveller taking major road, getting charitable donation?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI
a grant is a sum given, as by a charity

explanation.surface: A traveller takes the motorway, hoping for a charitable handout.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person or animal that moves from one region to another.

clue.text: Herald of the gods or some other messenger?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The gods' herald, or perhaps just another messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'or'; that word only links the definition to the wordplay, so it is left out.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hermes is the messenger and herald of the Olympian deities.

clue.text: Philosopher borders on optimistic, leading academic stream

indicators.note: leading means these letters come before the next piece
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken for its outside letters
the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge, a university town

explanation.surface: A philosopher verges on optimism, leading the academic stream of thought.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Occam (also Ockham) was a medieval English philosopher, known for Occam's razor.
explanation.definitionFit: Occam was a fourteenth-century English friar and thinker famous for his principle of parsimony.

clue.text: Singer who, over the years, changed the face of rock

definitions.text: Singer who, over the years, changed
definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... Richard, the British pop singer who changed with the times
second meaning: a steep rock face

explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a long-running British pop star. The surface suggests he changed rock music; a cliff is literally a face of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliff is a steep vertical rock face, and Cliff Richard is the singer named.

clue.text: Noble person will be denied this if buried at sea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a German count with territorial jurisdiction

definitions.text: will be denied this if buried at sea
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a burial at sea means no grave on land

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into LAND and GRAVE, which is exactly what a burial at sea lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a medieval German count ruling a territory, a title of nobility.

clue.text: Article about pub on street being "most deficient"

indicators.note: on means placed next to the following piece
about means around, so the article goes round the pub

parts.note: the is the definite article
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A newspaper article describing a pub on a street as the worst of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinnest can mean the most lacking in substance, the sparsest or poorest.

clue.text: Nothing is cleaner!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a space empty of all matter
second meaning: a ... cleaner, the household appliance

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a boast that nothing cleans better; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum is empty space, and the word is also short for the electric suction cleaner.

clue.text: Defence, brilliant, that is protecting lively man

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or brilliant

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the abbreviation wraps round the man

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a lad is a lively young man

explanation.surface: A brilliant defence, protecting a lively young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Defilade is a military term for arranging fortifications to shield troops from enemy fire.

clue.text: Says entrance is denied to clubs

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter, which is refused

parts.note: putters are golf clubs

explanation.surface: Someone reports that entry is refused to members of certain clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs or the card suit; it is golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or say aloud, so utters is a synonym of says.
